itinerary.cal: Season is July to August. This is a committing three-day glacier trip with essentially no bailout once past the Imperfect Impasse.
itinerary.totalNote: Three days: a full day in to Perfect Pass, a glacier-and-rock summit day on Poltergeist Pinnacle and Mount Challenger, and a day out.

days.title: Hike in to Perfect Pass
days.objective: Reach camp at Perfect Pass
days.note: Hike roughly 16 miles from the Hannegan Pass Trailhead via Hannegan Pass, the Chilliwack River ford, Easy Ridge and the Imperfect Impasse to camp at Perfect Pass. It is a full day with about 7,000 ft of gain.

days.title: Climb Poltergeist Pinnacle and Challenger
days.objective: Summit Poltergeist Pinnacle and Mount Challenger
days.note: Rope up and cross the Challenger Glacier to the base of Poltergeist Pinnacle, roughly 3 hours from camp per the first-ascent account. Climb the East Face route (3 technical pitches plus about 800 ft of simul-climbed ridge) and traverse to Mount Challenger's summit. Descend the Challenger Glacier back to camp at Perfect Pass.

days.title: Hike out to the trailhead
days.objective: Return to the Hannegan Pass Trailhead
days.note: Hike out from Perfect Pass to the trailhead, reversing the approach over Easy Ridge, the Chilliwack River and Hannegan Pass.

figureSources: D1 miles/gain prose; D1 loss row (gain minus net rise, TH 3110 to Perfect Pass 6300); D2 gain/loss row (Perfect Pass 6300 to summit 8200), miles row approach (~3 mi glacier each way); D3 mirrors D1; hours null (prose says only 'full day'); packs estimated
notes: Dropped 'Drive to the Hannegan Pass Trailhead' (road). Row dist_km 4.8 cannot be the trip distance (prose: ~16 mi one way); row gain_ft 7066 matches the approach day only, not the round trip. Day 3 prose is only 'Hike out to the trailhead'; route wording added from the Day 1 prose.

itinerary.cal: Season is July to August. Faster alternatives are an out-and-back from Cascade Pass (4-5 days), or extend the trip to the Dome Peak summit and add Sentinel Peak/Old Guard (7-8 days). Dome Peak (8,924 ft) is climbed from the Itswoot Ridge camp via the Dome Glacier route (35-degree snow and ice) as an extra day after Day 5.
itinerary.totalNote: A six-day north-to-south traverse from Cascade Pass to Downey Creek, camping at Kool-Aid Lake, Yang-Yang Lakes, White Rock Lakes (with a rest day) and Itswoot Ridge.

days.title: Cascade Pass to Kool-Aid Lake
days.objective: Cross Cache Col to the Kool-Aid Lake bivouac
days.note: Hike the Cascade Pass Trail 3.7 miles to the pass, then go off-trail south and cross Cache Col on the Cache Glacier. Descend to the Kool-Aid Lake bivouac at about 6,100 ft; expect 4-6 hours and about 3,300 ft of gain.

days.title: Kool-Aid Lake to Yang-Yang Lakes
days.objective: Cross Red Ledge and Spider-Formidable Col
days.note: Cross the exposed Red Ledge below Art's Knoll (Class 3 scrambling) and climb the Middle Cascade Glacier to Spider-Formidable Col. Descend to the Yang-Yang Lakes bivouac; plan on 8-11 hours with about 2,500 ft of gain and loss.

days.title: Yang-Yang Lakes to White Rock Lakes
days.objective: Traverse Le Conte Ridge and Glacier
days.note: Traverse Le Conte Ridge and cross the Le Conte Glacier, which has crevasse hazards. Descend to the White Rock Lakes bivouac, the visual highlight of the route; plan on 7-11 hours with about 2,000 ft of gain and loss.

days.title: Rest day at White Rock Lakes
days.objective: Rest or take a peak day
days.note: Day 4 is an optional rest day or peak day at White Rock Lakes.

days.title: White Rock Lakes to Itswoot Ridge
days.objective: Cross the Dana Glacier past Spire Point
days.note: Ascend the Dana Glacier, crossing the bergschrund, then summit Spire Point (8,264 ft) or traverse below it on the east face. Descend to the Itswoot Ridge bivouac; plan on 8-10 hours with about 3,000 ft of gain.

days.title: Itswoot Ridge to Downey Creek
days.objective: Hike out to the Downey Creek Trailhead
days.note: Descend Bachelor Creek through forest and follow the trail out to the Downey Creek Trailhead. Plan on 8-12 hours.

figureSources: gain/hours prose (ranges -> midpoints); D1 loss row (Cache Col 6903 to Kool-Aid 6120); D5 loss row (6200+3000-6400); D6 miles/gain/loss web (Abegg Downey TH-Itswoot 12.8 mi +5700/-800, reversed), hours prose; D1-D5 miles not found per day (route total ~30 mi per row dist_km 48.3 km and Abegg)
notes: Prose Day 6 says ~2,500 ft loss; that contradicts waypoints (Itswoot camp 6,400 ft to Downey TH ~1,450 ft) and Abegg (-5,700 ft), so the number was left out of the note and the figure uses the derived loss. Prose Dome Peak 8,924 ft vs waypoint 8,920 ft. Day 4 rest-day figures set to 0.

itinerary.cal: Season is July to September. The traverse is commonly done either as a long single day (about 13-14 hours car-to-car) from Easy Pass, or as the two-day trip below.
itinerary.totalNote: Two days: approach to a high camp on Mesahchie's south shoulder, then traverse Mesahchie, Katsuk, Kimtah and Cosho and hike out via Fisher Creek.

days.title: Approach to Mesahchie high camp
days.objective: Reach high camp at about 6,700 ft
days.note: Approach via Easy Pass and Fisher Creek to a high camp at about 6,700 ft on Mesahchie Peak's south shoulder.

days.title: Traverse Mesahchie to Cosho and hike out
days.objective: Traverse four summits and descend to Fisher Creek
days.note: Traverse Mesahchie, Katsuk, Kimtah and Cosho, then descend to the Fisher Creek trail. Follow the trail out over Easy Pass to the trailhead.

figureSources: no per-day figures in prose; row gain_ft null; row approach gives ~5 hr to camp but for the south-side sidehill route, not the Fisher Creek approach in the prose, so not used; web searches found no per-day stats (CascadeClimbers TRs blocked)
notes: Day 2 'out over Easy Pass to the trailhead' comes from the row descent. Row dist_km 33.8 km (~21 mi) looks like a full loop round trip. Row approach describes the high camp as reached by sidehilling from Easy Pass (~5 hr), while prose says via Easy Pass and Fisher Creek.

itinerary.cal: Season is June to September. Most parties climb Rampage alone as a long single day car-to-car, or link it with a Burgundy Spire route such as Action Potential for a bigger day. One documented Burgundy linkup ran from roughly 6 AM to just before 7 PM (about 13 hours) for 12 combined pitches.
itinerary.totalNote: A long single day car-to-car to climb the four-pitch Rampage on Paisano Pinnacle.

days.title: Climb Rampage car-to-car
days.objective: Climb Rampage on Paisano Pinnacle
days.note: Hike the Wine Spires trail past the bench camp toward Burgundy Col, then traverse the ledge system to the base and climb the four pitches of Rampage. Descend by scrambling toward Burgundy Spire's north face or making two 30 m rappels to Burgundy Col, then return to the car.

figureSources: gain row; miles row (dist_km 3.5 one-way x2); hours null (only the 13-hr figure for a linkup is given)
notes: Day note built from the row approach/descent because the prose itself only says 'long single day'. The 6 AM-7 PM times describe a Burgundy linkup, so they went in cal, not the schedule.

itinerary.cal: Season is June to October. The documented winter ascent (Gilbertson and Robinson, January 2019) skied in to camp at Crater Lake, summited and returned to camp the same day, then skied out the next day. A summer visit via the maintained Crater Creek/Crater Lakes Trail can be done as a single long day or a lighter two-day trip with a camp at the lake; the two-day version is laid out below.
itinerary.totalNote: A lighter two-day trip: hike in to Crater Lake, then climb the southeast ridge and hike out.

days.title: Hike in to Crater Lake
days.objective: Camp at Lower Crater Lake
days.note: Hike the maintained Crater Creek/Crater Lakes Trail about 3.9 miles to camp at Lower Crater Lake (7.8 miles round trip).

days.title: Climb the southeast ridge and hike out
days.objective: Summit Raven Ridge and return to the trailhead
days.note: Climb from the lake basin to the ~8,000 ft col and scramble the southeast ridge to the summit. Reverse the ridge to camp and hike out the Crater Creek Trail.

figureSources: D1 miles prose (7.8 RT), gain row approach (~2,100 ft); D2 gain row (summit 8572 minus lake ~6840), loss = D2 gain + D1 gain; D2 miles null (off-trail distance not given); hours null
notes: Dropped 'from an unplowed road' (road). Day 2 route detail from the row approach/descent. Row gain_ft 3822 matches D1+D2 gain.

itinerary.cal: Season is late May to October. Parties combining Raven Ridge with Hoodoo Peak often backpack about 5 miles in to camp near the old cabin (about 7,170 ft) or at Libby Lake, climb both peaks via the connecting ridge on day two, and hike out on day three; fit, fast parties do it as a very long single day.
itinerary.totalNote: A single long day from the Libby Lake Trailhead, about 12-13 miles round trip with 4,200 ft of gain.

days.title: Climb Raven Ridge from Libby Lake
days.objective: Summit Raven Ridge and return
days.note: Most parties climb Raven Ridge as a single long day from the Libby Lake Trailhead, roughly 12-13 miles round trip with about 4,200 ft of gain. Hike to Libby Lake, climb the talus gully and ridge scramble to the summit, and reverse the route to the trailhead.

figureSources: miles/gain prose (row dist_km 10.5 one-way agrees); hours null
notes: Route detail (talus gully, ridge scramble) from row approach/descent.

itinerary.cal: Season is July to September. The plan starts at Remmel Lake, which is itself a long backpack from the trailhead.
itinerary.totalNote: Two days from Remmel Lake: bushwhack to a high camp on the lower NW ridge, then climb, rappel and return to Remmel Lake.

days.title: Bushwhack to the NW ridge camp
days.objective: Camp at 7,500 ft on the lower ridge
days.note: From Remmel Lake, bushwhack south through forests and bogs to camp at 7,500 ft on the lower ridge.

days.title: Climb the NW Ridge and return
days.objective: Summit Remmel and return to Remmel Lake
days.note: Climb from camp to the summit, typically about 3.5 hours. Rappel and descend back to camp in about 2.5 hours, then return to Remmel Lake.

figureSources: D1 miles row approach (~2 mi), gain row (camp 7500 minus Remmel Lake 6868); D2 gain row (8685-7500), loss to Remmel Lake; D2 hours left null because prose's 6 hr covers only camp-summit-camp, not the walk back to Remmel Lake
notes: Prose omits the approach to Remmel Lake from the Andrews Creek Trailhead; row gain_ft 5265 and dist_km 28.2 seem to include it, so day figures don't sum to the row totals. The cal line noting the long approach to Remmel Lake is added context from the row, not the prose.

itinerary.cal: Season is July to September. This is typically a 2-3 day backpack; strong parties have also done the whole round trip (25+ miles, 5,500-6,800 ft of gain) as a single very long day.
itinerary.totalNote: Three days: hike in to Four Point Lake, walk up Remmel Mountain from camp, and hike out.

days.title: Hike in to Four Point Lake
days.objective: Camp at Four Point Lake
days.note: Hike in along the Chewuch River and Four Point Creek trails to camp at Four Point Lake, or camp along the Chewuch or Andrews Creek trail.

days.title: Climb Remmel Mountain
days.objective: Summit and return to camp
days.note: Follow the abandoned Coleman Ridge Trail to a cairn at about 7,070 ft. Climb open meadow and talus on the unofficial path to the summit and return to camp.

days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to the trailhead
days.note: Hike out the same trails to the trailhead.

figureSources: D1/D3 miles web (Outbound: #505 junction ~mile 13 plus ~2 mi to lake via Thirtymile); D1 gain row net (Four Point Lake 6846 minus Thirtymile TH 3400; real gain higher); D2 gain row (8685-6846), miles web-derived (Outbound 16.6 mi one-way to summit minus ~15); hours null
notes: Distance sources disagree: prose says 25+ mi round trip, Outbound 33 mi, a WTA TR ~13 mi to the lake. Row dist_km 25.7 km (~16 mi) fits a one-way distance to the summit. Day 2 route detail from row approach.

itinerary.cal: Season is July to September.
itinerary.totalNote: Four days: water taxi and Big Beaver valley to Luna Camp, up Access Creek to Luna Col, an East-to-West Fury traverse day, and the walk out.

days.title: Water taxi and hike to Luna Camp
days.objective: Reach Luna Camp
days.note: Take the water taxi from Ross Dam to the Big Beaver landing, then hike 9.4 miles up the Big Beaver Trail to Luna Camp.

days.title: Climb Access Creek to Luna Col
days.objective: Reach high camp at Luna Col
days.note: Climb Access Creek and over Access Col to a high camp at Luna Col (about 7,200 ft).

days.title: Traverse East Fury to West Fury
days.objective: Summit East and West Fury
days.note: From Luna Col, ascend East Fury, traverse to West Fury, and return over East Fury to Luna Col.

days.title: Hike out to Ross Lake
days.objective: Catch the water taxi back
days.note: Descend Access Creek and the Big Beaver Trail to Ross Lake for the water taxi return.

figureSources: D1 miles prose; D2 gain / D4 loss row (Luna Col 7200 minus Luna Camp 2432, net); other figures not found (Fury trip pages fetched had no per-day stats)
notes: Row dist_km 0.5 is far too short for the trip (Big Beaver alone is 9.4 mi); row gain_ft null. D4 is long (Luna Col to the landing, 9.4 mi plus Access Creek).

itinerary.cal: Season is July to September. Center Stage pairs with Flight of the Falcon on Salish Peak for a big linkup for fast, motivated parties.
itinerary.totalNote: A single long day: a 3-3.5 hour approach, 10 pitches, a rappel descent and a 3-3.5 hour exit, with an optional bivy at the base the night before.

days.title: Climb Center Stage on the Roan Wall
days.objective: Climb 10 pitches and rappel the route
days.note: Approach about 3-3.5 hours to the base, climb the full 10 pitches, and rappel the route on its bolted double-ring anchors. The exit takes another 3-3.5 hours. To shorten the climbing day, bivy at the Martha's Place boulder near the base the night before.

figureSources: gain row; approach/exit hours prose (MP agrees: 3-3.5 hr approach) but climbing time not given, so total hours null; miles not found
notes: Row gain_ft 3800 looks high against the trailhead (1,100 ft) and basin base (2,659 ft) waypoints plus a ~10-pitch route. Row approach road/washout lines were not in the prose.

itinerary.cal: Season is July to September.
itinerary.totalNote: A long single day: the 3-3.5 hour approach shared with Center Stage, 10 pitches, and a rappel descent down Center Stage, with an optional bivy at the base the night before.

days.title: Climb Stage Right on the Roan Wall
days.objective: Climb 10 pitches and rappel Center Stage
days.note: Approach about 3-3.5 hours to the base (shared with Center Stage) and climb the full 10 pitches. Descend by rappelling Center Stage's bolted anchors. To shorten the climbing day, bivy at Martha's Place near the base the night before.

figureSources: gain row; approach hours prose but total day hours not given; miles not found
notes: Same gain_ft concern as Center Stage (3,800 ft vs trailhead 1,100 ft and base 2,659 ft).

itinerary.cal: Season is late June to September. The climb can also be done as an overnight, camping at the Southeast Robinson Tarn (or lower in the Beauty Creek valley or at the Robinson Creek bridge) to split the approach and summit push.
itinerary.totalNote: A very long single day: about 14-15 miles round trip and 6,100-6,500 ft of gain, around 12 hours car-to-car.

days.title: Climb Robinson Mountain car-to-car
days.objective: Summit via the southeast ridge and return
days.note: Climb the southeast ridge as a very long single day, about 14-15 miles round trip with 6,100-6,500 ft of gain. Reported car-to-car times are around 12 hours.

figureSources: miles/hours prose; gain row (within prose range)

itinerary.cal: Season is June to September. The distance and elevation figures describe the entire three-peak Nason Ridge traverse, not an isolated Rock Mountain ascent.
itinerary.totalNote: A two-day, roughly 15-mile traverse over Mount Mastiff and Mount Howard to camp in the Upper Canaan Lake basin, then over Rock Mountain and out to US-2.

days.title: Merritt Lake over Mastiff and Howard
days.objective: Camp in the Upper Canaan Lake basin
days.note: Hike from the Old Merritt Lake Trailhead to Merritt Lake, then continue over Mount Mastiff and Mount Howard to camp in the Upper Canaan Lake basin at about 6,050 ft. This day accumulates about 6,000 ft of gain.

days.title: Climb Rock Mountain and descend
days.objective: Summit Rock Mountain and exit to US-2
days.note: Cross the Howard-Rock col and climb Rock Mountain's northeast side. Descend the South Ridge-East Slope past Rock Lake and out the Rock Mountain Trail to the US-2 trailhead; the full traverse totals roughly 6,300 ft of loss.

figureSources: D1 gain prose; D1 loss row-derived (6000 minus net rise, TH 2950 from approach to camp 6050); D2 loss = prose total 6300 minus D1 loss; per-day miles not split (prose total ~15 mi)
notes: Row gain_ft and dist_km are null. Total ~15 mi not split between days.

itinerary.cal: Season is July to September. Strong parties can also do the climb as a single very long day.
itinerary.totalNote: Two days: hike to Fourth of July Camp, then summit Ruby Mountain and hike all the way out.

days.title: Hike in to Fourth of July Camp
days.objective: Set up camp at Fourth of July Camp
days.note: Hike 4.8 miles and about 2,300 ft from the trailhead to Fourth of July Camp (about 2.7 hours) and set up camp. There is a permanent water source at camp, but none higher on the mountain by mid-summer.

days.title: Summit Ruby and hike out
days.objective: Climb the south ridge and return to the trailhead
days.note: Climb from camp to the summit, about 4,000 ft of gain in roughly 6.1 hours. Return to camp in about 3.6 hours, then hike out to the trailhead in about 1.7 hours.

figureSources: gain/hours prose; D1 miles prose; D2 miles row-derived (dist_km 13.7 = 8.5 mi one-way; 2x(8.5-4.8)+4.8)
notes: Row gain_ft 6300 = 2,300 + 4,000. Minor: row high_point_ft 7408 vs summit waypoint 7426.

itinerary.cal: Season is July to September.
itinerary.totalNote: A single long day from Longmire to the Eagle Peak-Chutla saddle and up the ridge scramble, about 7-9 miles and 3,200 ft round trip.

days.title: Scramble Eagle Peak from Longmire
days.objective: Summit Eagle Peak and return
days.note: Hike about 3.6 miles one way and 2,900 ft up to the Eagle Peak-Chutla saddle, then scramble the ridge to the summit for another 250-300 ft of gain over uneven terrain. Reverse the full route to the trailhead, about 7-9 miles and 3,200 ft round trip depending on the line taken.

figureSources: miles/gain prose (WTA: saddle 7.2 mi RT, 2,910 ft, consistent); hours not found
notes: Row gain_ft 3297 vs prose ~3,200 (close).

itinerary.cal: Season is June to September.
itinerary.totalNote: A long single day: a short approach, 7 pitches up the Shield Wall, rappels through the gendarmes, 6 more pitches to the summit and the standard-route descent.

days.title: Climb the Shield Wall and SE Ridge
days.objective: Summit Mount Washington via the SE Ridge
days.note: Approach roughly 1-1.25 hours from the trailhead to the base and climb 7 pitches (low 5th class to 5.7) up the Shield Wall. Make up to three 30 m rappels through the ridge's gendarmes and climb about 6 more pitches (3rd class to 5.7) to the summit. Descend via the standard route back to the car.

figureSources: gain row; hours web (Sverdina 2007 TR: ~2 hr to base, almost 8 hr on route, 1:45 summit to cars); miles not found
notes: Hours from a single trip report; faster parties report ~6 hr car to summit.

itinerary.cal: Season is May to June.
itinerary.totalNote: Camp in the basin below the couloir, climb the Northeast Couloir to the Balanced Rock summit, and hike out.

days.title: Approach to camp below the couloir
days.objective: Camp between Sherpa and Argonaut
days.note: Approach from the Stuart Lake Trailhead to a camp in the basin between Sherpa and Argonaut, below the couloir.

days.title: Climb the Northeast Couloir
days.objective: Reach the Balanced Rock summit
days.note: Make an alpine start and climb the couloir (snow and ice to roughly 50 degrees) to its top, then scramble up and right to the Balanced Rock summit via a short 5.0 pitch. Descend the same route, or go around to Sherpa Pass and downclimb from there to camp.

days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to the Stuart Lake Trailhead
days.note: Hike back out to the Stuart Lake Trailhead.

figureSources: D2 gain/loss row (summit 8630 minus camp bench 5400); trailhead elevation and distances missing from row, not found
notes: Prose gives no day split and no hike-out; Day 3 hike-out was inferred (could be done on Day 2). Row gain_ft/dist_km null.

itinerary.cal: Season is May to July. The approach is the same multi-day approach used for the Southwest Route, typically 2-3 days to a high camp near Itswoot Ridge or the Dome Glacier, with 1-2 more days to reverse it.
itinerary.totalNote: Four days from Downey Creek: two days in to a high camp near the Dome Glacier, a climbing day on the north face, and a long day out.

days.title: Downey Creek to Itswoot Ridge
days.objective: Camp on Itswoot Ridge
days.note: Begin the approach shared with the Southwest Route, hiking from the Downey Creek Trailhead up Bachelor Creek to camp on Itswoot Ridge.

days.title: Move up to the Dome Glacier high camp
days.objective: Reach high camp near the Dome Glacier
days.note: Continue from Itswoot Ridge to a high camp near the Dome Glacier.

days.title: Climb the North Face
days.objective: Summit Sinister Peak via the north face
days.note: From high camp, cross the Dome-Chickamin col (about 8,500 ft), descend onto the Chickamin Glacier, and climb the north face directly to the summit. Return to camp.

days.title: Hike out to Downey Creek
days.objective: Return to the Downey Creek Trailhead
days.note: Reverse the approach to the Downey Creek Trailhead; some parties take two days for this.

figureSources: D1, D2, D4 web (Abegg Gunsight trip from the same Downey Creek / Itswoot / Dome-Chickamin col camps: 12.8 mi +5700/-800 ~10 hr; 3.2 mi +2500/-250 ~3 hr; out 16 mi +1050/-8200 ~12.5 hr); D3 not found
notes: Prose gives no day split; 2 approach days + climb + 1 out chosen from the prose's 2-3 / 1-2 day ranges. D1/D2 route wording from row approach/bivy list. Row gain_ft/dist_km null.

itinerary.cal: Season is July to September. As a day trip, depart before dawn and allow 10-12 hours total.
itinerary.totalNote: Three days: hike in over Trap Pass to Trap Lake, climb Slippery Slab Tower from camp, and hike out.

days.title: Hike in to Trap Lake
days.objective: Camp at Trap Lake
days.note: Leave the Tunnel Creek Trailhead early and reach Hope Lake in 2-2.5 hours. Continue over Trap Pass and camp at Trap Lake just below it, another 2-3 hours of approach.

days.title: Climb Slippery Slab Tower
days.objective: Climb the NE Face and return to camp
days.note: Climb Slippery Slab Tower's NE Face and return to camp, about 6-8 hours. Descend with two rappels (60 m double-strand) and follow the boot path back over Trap Pass.

days.title: Hike out to the trailhead
days.objective: Return to the Tunnel Creek Trailhead
days.note: Return to the trailhead, about 4-5 hours.

figureSources: hours prose (ranges -> midpoints); D1/D3 miles and D1 gain web (WTA Trap Lake 11.0 mi RT, 2,700 ft); D1 loss row (Trap Pass 5772 to Trap Lake 5143); D2 gain row (summit 6361 minus Trap Lake 5143); D2 miles not found
notes: Descent detail in D2 from row descent. Row gain_ft 3300 is the one-way net-ish figure; cumulative is higher.

itinerary.cal: Season is July to September. The climb can be split over two days with a bivy at The Ledge (about 2 miles in) or at Burgundy Col itself (about 7,800 ft), a good base if linking Vasiliki with Burgundy Spire or other nearby Wine Spires towers.
itinerary.totalNote: Usually one long car-to-car day: 3-4 hours up to Burgundy Col, a few hours on the three-pitch South Face, and 3-4 hours back.

days.title: Climb Vasiliki Tower car-to-car
days.objective: Climb the South Face and return
days.note: Approach roughly 3-4 hours to Burgundy Col and climb the three-pitch South Face. Downclimb the North Ridge or rappel back to the col, then hike out the same way in another 3-4 hours.

figureSources: gain row; miles row (dist_km 4.8 one-way x2); hours null (prose: 6-8 hr approach/return plus 'a few hours' on route)
notes: Row high_point_ft 7663 vs summit waypoint 8062 and Burgundy Col 7800 - the high point looks wrong.

itinerary.cal: Season is July to September. This is one of the longest wilderness approaches in the state, around 18 miles one way.
itinerary.totalNote: Four days: hike in toward Upper Cathedral Lake, reach basecamp and scout, climb the South Face from camp, and hike out.

days.title: Hike in toward Upper Cathedral Lake
days.objective: Make progress toward the Upper Cathedral Lake basin
days.note: Hike in from the Andrews Creek Trailhead toward the Upper Cathedral Lake basin.

days.title: Reach basecamp, rest and scout
days.objective: Settle at Upper Cathedral Lake
days.note: Continue to basecamp at Upper Cathedral Lake if needed, then rest and scout the route.

days.title: Climb the South Face
days.objective: Summit Cathedral Peak and return to camp
days.note: Climb the seven-pitch South Face from camp and descend the standard southwest-slope walk-up back to camp.

days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to the Andrews Creek Trailhead
days.note: Hike the roughly 18 miles back to the Andrews Creek Trailhead.

figureSources: D3 gain row (summit 8601 minus camp 7400); D4 miles row (approach ~18 mi one way; dist_km 29 agrees); D1/D2 split of the 18 mi not stated
notes: Dropped 'drive to trailhead' (road). Prose's 'climb car-to-car from camp' read as camp-to-camp. Row gain_ft 4700 understates the route (approach crosses Andrews Pass and drops into Spanish Creek).

itinerary.cal: Season is June to October. In good conditions this is a half-day outing; one party in poor conditions (fog to 20 ft visibility, verglas, fresh snow) took most of a day.
itinerary.totalNote: A half day in good conditions: an hour's approach up Commonwealth, the South Gully past two chockstones, and the South Spur to the south summit.

days.title: Climb the South Gully to the south summit
days.objective: Reach Guye Peak's south summit
days.note: From the Summit West lot in firm winter snow, approach about an hour up Commonwealth to the base of the gully. Climb three rope lengths to the first chockstone, pass a second chockstone and the short ice or rock step above it, and continue out onto the South Spur to the south summit. For the full traverse, continue over the middle summit, make the rappel, and finish up the north summit before descending west to Alpental or east down Commonwealth.

figureSources: gain row; hours null ('half day' to 'most of a day'); miles not given
notes: Prose is a winter account while row season is Jun-Oct.

itinerary.cal: Season is June to October. Plan on a half day to a full day car to car; with the drive from Seattle under an hour, it is a realistic after-work or short-weather-window objective. No camping is needed or wanted.
itinerary.totalNote: A half to full day car-to-car: walk to the base, climb five pitches, and descend via the Southeast Couloir and Cave Ridge trail.

days.title: Climb the South Rib
days.objective: Reach Guye Peak's south summit
days.note: Park on Alpental Road, walk the ski track and boulder field to the base, and climb five pitches or simulclimb the easier ground. A fast party reached the south summit 1.5 hours after leaving the car, but a roped party of two should plan on the better part of a day. Descend north over the subsummits and out via the Southeast Couloir and the Cave Ridge trail.

figureSources: gain row; miles row (dist_km 4.83 taken as round trip - 3 mi one-way is implausible for this roadside crag); hours null (prose: half to full day)
notes: Row dist_km 4.83 appears to be round trip.

itinerary.cal: Season is July to September. Plan 1-2 days of approach, a climbing day, and 1-2 days out. South Peak can be reached from Stehekin (ferry up Lake Chelan, shuttle to High Bridge) or from Downey Creek in the west; this plan uses the Downey Creek approach.
itinerary.totalNote: Four days from Downey Creek: two approach days to a high camp near the Dome-Chickamin col, a climbing day on the South Ridge, and a long day out.

days.title: Downey Creek to Itswoot Ridge
days.objective: Camp on Itswoot Ridge
days.note: Hike from the Downey Creek Trailhead up Bachelor Creek past Cub Lake to camp on Itswoot Ridge.

days.title: Move up to the Dome Glacier high camp
days.objective: Reach the Dome-Chickamin col high camp
days.note: Continue from Itswoot Ridge across the glacier to a high bivouac near the Dome Glacier and the Dome-Chickamin col.

days.title: Climb the South Ridge
days.objective: Summit South Peak and return to camp
days.note: Climb the three-pitch South Ridge to the summit. Do not reverse the ridge; rappel about 35 m north off the top, make a second rappel east onto the Blue Glacier, and return to camp.

days.title: Hike out to Downey Creek
days.objective: Return to the Downey Creek Trailhead
days.note: Reverse the approach to the Downey Creek Trailhead.

figureSources: D1, D2, D4 web (Abegg trip to the Gunsight Range from the same camps); D3 not found
notes: Prose gives no day split; route detail from row approach/descent/bivy. Ferry/shuttle mention kept in cal (transport, not road). Row dist_km null; row gain_ft 7000.

itinerary.cal: Season is July to September.
itinerary.totalNote: Three days: approach to the Eldorado high camp, climb the South Ridge and descend the East Ridge, then hike out.

days.title: Hike in to Eldorado high camp
days.objective: Reach high camp at about 7,600 ft
days.note: Approach via Eldorado Creek and the Eldorado Glacier to high camp at about 7,600 ft, which takes 5-6 hours.

days.title: Climb the South Ridge
days.objective: Summit Eldorado and return to camp
days.note: Climb the four-pitch South Ridge and descend the East Ridge back to camp.

days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to the trailhead
days.note: Hike out from high camp to the trailhead.

figureSources: D1 hours prose; gain/loss row (camp 7600 minus TH 2164; summit 8868 minus camp); miles not split (WTA: 10.0 mi RT to summit, 6,716 ft)
notes: Row gain_ft 6800 matches ~6,710 summed. Total ~10 mi RT per WTA but per-day split not found.

itinerary.cal: Season is June to September.
itinerary.totalNote: Two days: hike in to Boston Basin high camp, then climb the South Ridge and descend the North Ridge to camp.

days.title: Hike in to Boston Basin high camp
days.objective: Reach high camp at about 6,400 ft
days.note: Hike the Boston Basin climbers' path to high camp at about 6,400 ft.

days.title: Climb the South Ridge
days.objective: Summit Aiguille de l'M and return to camp
days.note: Make an early start, approach via snowfields to the base of the South Ridge, and climb the 5 pitches to the top. Descend via the North Ridge back to camp, with one short rappel from fixed slings.

figureSources: gain/loss row (camp 6400 minus TH 3200; summit 7200 minus camp); miles/hours not found from an opened source
notes: Dropped 'Drive to the Boston Basin trailhead' (road). Prose ends at camp; the hike out is not given, so days do not sum to a round trip. Waypoint high camp 6,250 ft vs prose 6,400 ft. Row gain_ft 4000 = 3,200 + 800.

itinerary.cal: Season is July to September. This is typically a 2-3 day trip; the descent to the trailhead can also be done on the summit day.
itinerary.totalNote: Two to three days: approach to a high bivy, climb the Southeast Ridge from the Pyramid notch, and descend to the trailhead.

days.title: Approach to high camp
days.objective: Reach a bivy below the Sulphide Glacier
days.note: Approach to a bivy near Winnie's Slide or at the Sulphide high camp.

days.title: Climb the Southeast Ridge
days.objective: Summit Mount Shuksan
days.note: Make an alpine start, cross the glaciers to the Pyramid notch, and climb the Southeast Ridge to the summit. Rappel back to the notch and return to camp.

days.title: Descend to the trailhead
days.objective: Hike out to the trailhead
days.note: Descend from camp to the trailhead.

figureSources: gain/loss row (Sulphide camp 6400 minus Shannon Ridge TH 2500; summit 9131 minus camp); miles not split (row dist_km 11.3 = ~7 mi one-way to summit); hours not from an opened source
notes: Contradiction: prose says bivy 'near Winnie's Slide', which is on the Fisher Chimneys/Lake Ann approach, while the row approach and camps are Shannon Ridge/Sulphide Glacier. Row gain_ft 6627 matches 3,900 + 2,730.

itinerary.cal: Season is June to September.
itinerary.totalNote: Three days: backpack up Ingalls Creek and Crystal Creek, climb the roughly 19-pitch Southwest Rib, and hike out.

days.title: Hike in to Crystal Creek Basin
days.objective: Camp in Crystal Creek Basin or at Crystal Lake
days.note: Backpack in via the Ingalls Creek Trail and the Crystal Creek/Nightmare Gorge boot path to a camp in Crystal Creek Basin or at Crystal Lake.

days.title: Climb the Southwest Rib
days.objective: Summit Crystal Lake Tower and return to camp
days.note: Climb the Southwest Rib (roughly 19 pitches) to the summit. Descend via the Westernmost Chessman to the Enchantment Plateau or back to Crystal Lake, then return to camp.

days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to the Ingalls Creek Trailhead
days.note: Hike out via Crystal Creek and the Ingalls Creek Trail to the trailhead.

figureSources: camp elevation unknown (row bivy elev null), so no per-day gain split; web search suggests the Crystal Creek turnoff is ~7-7.5 mi up Ingalls Creek but no page confirming it could be opened (SummitPost/CascadeClimbers 403)
notes: Dropped 'Drive to Ingalls Creek Trailhead' (road). Row high_point_ft 7923 vs summit waypoint 7800. Row gain_ft 6000 not split.

itinerary.cal: Season is July to September. Treat this as a long day or an overnight: the first-ascent party needed 7-8 hours on the route alone and bivied at the summit after arriving in the dark.
itinerary.totalNote: A long single day (or an overnight with a summit bivy) to climb the 9-pitch East Face and descend the standard route over Headlee Pass.

days.title: Climb the East Face of Sperry Peak
days.objective: Summit Sperry Peak via the East Face
days.note: From below the east face, scramble up through brush and easy rock to the obvious slabby face just left of the small pocket glacier. Climb about 9 pitches, allowing 7-8 hours on the route, then descend the standard west-ridge/southwest-slope route to Lake Elan and out over Headlee Pass.

figureSources: miles/gain web (WTA Sperry Peak standard route: 6.4 mi RT, 3,800 ft, approximate for this line); hours null (only route time 7-8 hr given)
notes: Row gain/dist/high point and waypoints all null; descent in row is marked 'not known in detail'. WTA summit 6,120 ft.

itinerary.cal: Season is July to September. Plan on most of a day.
itinerary.totalNote: A full day: approach to Headlee Pass, climb 8 pitches/sections of low-5th rock on the upper South Ridge, and descend the standard route.

days.title: Climb Sperry's Upper South Ridge
days.objective: Summit Sperry Peak via the South Ridge
days.note: Approach to Headlee Pass as for the standard route, cross the talus toward Vesper/Elan Lake, and take the first ramp up and right to the base of the South Ridge. Climb the 8 pitches/sections of low-5th climbing and scrambling. Descend to the west to the Vesper-Sperry saddle, then south back to Headlee Pass and out to the trailhead.

figureSources: miles/gain web (WTA Sperry Peak standard route, approximate); hours null ('most of a day')
notes: Route detail from row approach/descent. Row gain/dist/high point null.

itinerary.cal: Season is July to September. Many parties combine Spider Mountain with Mount Formidable from the same camp.
itinerary.totalNote: Three days: hike over Cache Col to Kool-Aid Lake, climb Spider Mountain from camp, and hike out.

days.title: Hike in to Kool-Aid Lake
days.objective: Camp at Kool-Aid Lake or Spider-Formidable Col
days.note: Hike from the Cascade Pass Trailhead via Cascade Pass and Cache Col to a base camp at Kool-Aid Lake or Spider-Formidable Col, roughly 6-8 miles.

days.title: Climb Spider Mountain
days.objective: Summit via the southeast gully and east ridge
days.note: Climb Spider Mountain via the southeast gully and east ridge, about 3 hours from the col to the summit and roughly 8 hours round trip from Kool-Aid Lake. Downclimb the same buttress and gully back to the col and return to camp.

days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to the Cascade Pass Trailhead
days.note: Hike out over Cache Col and Cascade Pass to the trailhead.

figureSources: D1/D3 miles prose (6-8 mi); D2 hours prose; gain/loss row (TH 3600, Cache Col ~6900, Kool-Aid 6120, summit 8317)
notes: Dropped 'Drive to Cascade Pass Trailhead' (road). Row approach puts the Kool-Aid basin at ~6,800 ft vs bivy/waypoint 6,120 ft. Row gain_ft 4717 is the net TH-to-summit rise. D2 downclimb detail from row descent.

itinerary.cal: Season is June to October. Full car-to-car days of 9+ hours are commonly reported.
itinerary.totalNote: A full day car-to-car: a short approach, 6-7 pitches on the arete, and a rappel or gully descent.

days.title: Climb Spontaneity Arete car-to-car
days.objective: Climb the arete and return to the pullout
days.note: Start pre-dawn or early from the car and approach about 1-1.5 hours to the base. Allow roughly 4-6 hours for the 6-7 pitches, including route-finding and scrambling between belays. The rappel or gully descent back to the creek crossing and pullout takes 2-3+ hours.

figureSources: hours prose (9+ commonly reported); gain row; miles not found

itinerary.cal: Season is July to September.
itinerary.totalNote: A shorter day than Spontaneity Arete: a 1.5-hour approach, 4 pitches, and a single-rope rappel descent.

days.title: Climb Spontaneous Distraction
days.objective: Climb 4 pitches and rappel
days.note: Approach roughly 1.5 hours, spend a few hours on the 4 pitches, and make a comparatively quick single-rope rappel descent. It is a shorter day overall than the neighboring Spontaneity Arete.

figureSources: gain row; hours null ('a few hours' on route); miles not found
notes: Row gain_ft 1800 identical to Spontaneity Arete although this route is 4 pitches vs 7.

itinerary.cal: Season is July to September.
itinerary.totalNote: Three days: backpack to Fish Creek Pass, climb the Northwest Ridge as a long technical day from camp, and hike out.

days.title: Hike in to Fish Creek Pass
days.objective: Camp near Fish Creek Pass or at Star Lake
days.note: Backpack in on the West Fork Buttermilk Creek Trail to a camp at Star Lake or near Fish Creek Pass.

days.title: Climb the Northwest Ridge
days.objective: Summit Star Peak via the ridge
days.note: Climb the ridge as a technical day trip from camp, allowing a full day for the approach and the ridge's sustained, low-angle length before the crux. The descent off the ridge is undocumented, so settle on a strategy (downclimb or rappel the ridge, or drop west to the Southwest Spur scramble) before committing above the steep final section.

days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to the West Fork Buttermilk Trailhead
days.note: Hike back out the West Fork Buttermilk Creek Trail to the trailhead.

figureSources: D1/D3 miles and gain row approach (7 mi, 3,500 ft to Fish Creek Pass 7480); D2 gain row (8693-7480)
notes: Prose has no hike-out; Day 3 was inferred. Prose allows camping at Star Lake, but the row approach says not to descend to Star Lake for this route (figures assume Fish Creek Pass). Descent-strategy sentence from row descent. Row gain_ft 4800 matches 3,500 + 1,210.

itinerary.cal: Season is June to September.
itinerary.totalNote: A single day from Mazama: a 20-25 minute approach, five pitches to the clifftop, and a rappel descent.

days.title: Climb Summertime
days.objective: Climb 5 pitches and rappel
days.note: From the highway pullout near Mazama, approach about 20-25 minutes to the crag. Climb 5 pitches (Grade II, about 400 ft) of mixed bolts and trad gear to the clifftop, then rappel the route back to the base.

figureSources: gain row; hours/miles not given

itinerary.cal: Season is March to April.
itinerary.totalNote: Two days: approach up the Middle Fork Snoqualmie valley to camp below the north face, then climb the ~2,000 ft ice line, descend and hike out.

days.title: Approach to camp below the north face
days.objective: Establish camp below the north face
days.note: Bike or hike into the Middle Fork Snoqualmie valley, then continue on foot along the valley trail, fording the braids of the Middle Fork Snoqualmie River. Establish camp below the north face; the first-ascent party took about 6.5 hours from the vehicle.

days.title: Climb the north face and hike out
days.objective: Climb the ice line and return to the car
days.note: Make an alpine start around 6 AM and climb the roughly 2,000 ft ice line. Descend the southwest-side gully with two 30 m rappels and hike back out.

schedule.label: Alpine start
schedule.detail: Leave camp for the north face ice line.

figureSources: D1 hours prose; D2 start time prose; no gain/distance in prose or row (row gain/dist null, no waypoints)
notes: Dropped the 'drive the Middle Fork Snoqualmie Road' part of Day 1 (road). Valley/ford detail from row approach.
